y-m-38-01.material: Jeongeun class use cards numbered from 1. Dem put souvenir sticker on cards wey number divisible by 4 or by 6. Card wey divisible by both 4 and 6 still get only one sticker. Hayun calculate how many stickers dem need altogether for cards 1 through 50 as follows.

y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This no match the 3-person result we just see (4 ways and 2 ways). [3 4 2]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.info: Four people (Jisu, Minho, Sua, Hajun) fit stand 24 ways. Neighbors na 12 ways, apart too na 12. (4) [24 4 12 12]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: You check results for 3 and 4 people together. How about 5 or more? [3 4 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.after: With 4 people, the two case counts equal. The 3-person trend with neighbors ahead no continue straight. Only checking 5 or more fit show which side ahead. [4 3 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: From 3 to 4, gap between neighbor and apart shrink. If e keep growing, apart fit overtake neighbor. [3 4]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You predict direction by looking how the two results change.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Neighbor cases go continue to be at least as many as apart.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: E no clash with the two results so far, but e no account for the shrinking gap.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: With 3 people dem different: 4 ways and 2 ways. [3 4 2]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Equality with 4 people fit be chance. I go count 5 people myself to check. [4 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: This judgment careful; e no conclude from only two results.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Five people fit stand 120 ways. Treat Jisu and Minho as one block: 4 blocks arrange 24 ways; inside-block order get 2 ways, so neighbors na 48 ways and apart 72. (5) [120 5 24 4 2 48 72]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: You don see results for 3, 4, 5 people. What happen with plenty people, like 10 or 20? [3 4 5 10 20]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.after: With 5 people, apart pass neighbor for first time. Neighbor ratio dey shrink. Make we check 10 people directly? [5 10]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Apart go remain more, and gap from neighbor go widen.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You extend the three-result flow (neighbor ahead → equal → apart ahead) in your expectation.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Apart go be more, but ratio compared with neighbor hardly change.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Share of total that are neighbors dey shrink: 4/6 for 3 people, 12/24 for 4, 48/120 for 5. [4 6 3 12 24 4 48 120 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Some people count go make neighbor more again.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: The three results show no such trend. This expectation turn back without basis.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Hard to talk about 10 or 20 people from only three results. I go calculate direct to check. [10 20]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This judgment careful about generalizing from three examples.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.info: Ten people fit stand 3,628,800 ways. Neighbors: 2×9!=725,760; apart: 2,903,040, exactly 4 times neighbor. (10) [3 628 800 10 2 9 725 760 2 903 040 4]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.ask: To say if n ≥ 5 apart always more than neighbor, what basis best? [5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.after: More examples increase confidence, but “all n” settle only when you show expression that no depend on n. Neighbor share na 2/n of total, so n=4 exactly half; if n≥5 e less than half. [2 4 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.o.a: I check 5 people and 10 people, enough evidence; no need check more. [5 10]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.r.a: Two examples no represent all n. Examples only add evidence.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.o.b: Neighbors na 2/n of all (2×(n−1)!÷n!). If n ≥ 5, 2/n < 1/2. [2 2 1 5 2 1 2]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.r.b: This judgment build evidence using expression wey hold whatever n be.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.o.c: When people count grow, all cases increase, so apart must also become more than neighbor.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.r.c: Neighbor cases too increase when all cases increase, so that no basis to compare the two.
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.o.d: If I calculate n=20,30,50 directly too and get same result, I go conclude e always hold. [20 30 50]
y-m-38-03.s.s1.st.3.r.d: Good extra evidence, but plenty uncalculated n remain, so e no guarantee “always.”
y-m-38-03.s.s1.reflect: With 3 neighbor ahead, with 4 equal, and from 5 apart ahead. Whether you keep or change your first expectation, key point be say few examples make “always” hard to claim; expression independent of n fit settle am. [3 4 5]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.prompt: Of 120 arrangements for 5 people, Jisu and Minho apart in 72. Choose a method and explain with numbers why 72 come out. [120 5 72 72]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.hint.0: Decide whether e easier first count neighbor cases or first arrange nonadjacent places.
y-m-38-03.s.s2.hint.1: Write separately ways the other 3 people stand and places for the two people. [3]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: For each step of your method, numbers (24, 48, 6, 12, etc.) come out? You explain where dem come from? [24 48 6 12]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You remember Jisu and Minho order (2 ways)? [2]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You check whether another method also give 72? [72]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.model.0: First count neighbor cases. Treat the two as one block: 4 blocks line up 24 ways, with 2 internal orders, so 48. Subtract from total 120 to get 72. [24 4 2 48 48 120 72]
y-m-38-03.s.s2.model.1: First line up other 3 people, 6 ways. Place Jisu and Minho in two different spots among 4 gaps (between people and at ends): 4×3=12. Since dem no touch, 6×12=72 ways. [3 6 4 3 4 3 12 6 12 72]

y-m-38-04.title: Splitting 9 people into three teams of 3: why Seoyeon and Dohyeon answers differ [9 3]
y-m-38-04.topic: Splitting equal-size teams: when teams are distinguished or not
y-m-38-04.goal: Know that split-count changes depending on whether teams distinguished; explain how many times same split counted when not distinguished, and judge if same applies when team sizes all differ.
y-m-38-04.material: We want split 9 different club members into three teams of 3. Seoyeon say C(9,3)×C(6,3)×C(3,3)=84×20×1=1680 ways; Dohyeon say 1680÷6=280 ways. (C(9,3) counts ways to choose 3 of 9.) [9 3 9 3 6 3 3 3 84 20 1 1680 1680 6 280 9 3 3 9]
y-m-38-04.thinking.0: Find a condition missing from problem
y-m-38-04.thinking.1: Find the wrong line in solution
y-m-38-04.thinking.2: Explain why same case counted many times
y-m-38-04.prereq.0: H1 na production difficulty only, no grade assignment. Assume basic counting (split cases, successive choices, nPr and nCr) don learn. Combination C(n,r) count ways choose r of n, order no matter. [1]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.prompt: Which judgment about Seoyeon and Dohyeon answers best?
y-m-38-04.s.s1.hint.0: For small example, split 6 into three teams of 2 (가, 나, 다); write one split yourself. [6 2]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.hint.1: Count how many ways same split can be written by changing only team-name order.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.o.a: Seoyeon 1680 correct. Dohyeon division by 6 unnecessary. [1680 6]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.r.a: You miss say Seoyeon expression also distinguishes order teams chosen first.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.o.b: Dohyeon 280 correct. Same three teams count as one even if selection order different, so 1680 too many. [280 1680]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.r.b: You assume from start teams not distinguished. Check whether problem says so.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.o.c: Both wrong. Answer na 84, ways to choose one team. [84]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.r.c: 84 only fix one team. You no count task of fixing other teams. [84]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.o.d: Depending on whether teams distinguished, both values fit be answer.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.r.d: This judgment point out two answers came from different interpretations.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.explain: Seoyeon expression counts choosing first, second, third team in order, so teams distinguished (1680). If no names, orders of same three teams merge into one, giving 280. Problem no state this condition, so answer depend on it. [1680 280]
y-m-38-04.s.s1.acc.0: Natural to read unmarked “split into three teams” as teams not distinguished, but state the assumption.
y-m-38-04.s.s1.acc.1: If teams named Team 1, Team 2, Team 3, answer 1680. Problem no say this, so state your assumption. [1 2 3 1680]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.prompt: Suppose split six people into three teams of 2, teams indistinguishable. Find line where Jiho solution goes wrong. [2]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.hint.0: Check definition: C(6,2)=15 mean ways choose 2 people or ways line them up? [6 2 15 2 2]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.hint.1: For 6 people A-F, count how many times split {A,B},{C,D},{E,F} appear among 90. [6 90]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.line.0: Choose C(6,2)=15 first, then C(4,2)=6, then C(2,2)=1: total 15×6×1=90 if teams named. [6 2 15 4 2 6 2 2 1 15 6 1 90]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.line.1: Each team internal order has 2 ways, so divide by 2×2×2=8. [2 2 2 2 2 8]
y-m-38-04.s.s2.line.3: But count of ways must natural number; check calculation again.
y-m-38-04.s.s2.explain: Line 2 wrong. Combination C already ignores order of people chosen, so no need divide by within-team order. For unnamed teams divide by 3!=6, orders of selecting same teams. Then 90÷6=15; listing 6 people directly also give 15. Line 4 correctly notices line 3 is not natural count. [2 3 6 90 6 15 6 15 4 3]
y-m-38-04.s.s3.prompt: Now split 9 people into teams of 2,3,4, unnamed. Since teams indistinguishable, should divide by 3!? [9 2 3 4 3]
y-m-38-04.s.s3.hint.0: Write same split {가나},{다라마},{바사아자} with team order changed only. Are they different splits?
y-m-38-04.s.s3.hint.1: Write three team sizes side by side; check if any sizes same.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.o.a: We should divide. Teams unnamed, so same split counted 6 times. [6]
y-m-38-04.s.s3.r.a: You carry over rule from case all team sizes same.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.o.b: No divide. Team sizes different, so dem already distinguishable.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.r.b: You notice team size itself distinguish teams.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.o.c: Divide by 2!. Only swapping two teams make same split. [2]
y-m-38-04.s.s3.r.c: You no check which two teams have same size. All three sizes different.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.o.d: Whether to divide depends on team names, so we no know.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.r.d: Here even unnamed teams distinguished by size.
y-m-38-04.s.s3.explain: Teams of 2,3,4 already distinguished by size. Choose 2-person team C(9,2)=36 and 3-person team C(7,3)=35, rest team of 4; total 36×35=1260, no separate division needed. [2 3 4 2 9 2 36 3 7 3 35 4 36 35 1260]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.prompt: Explain why splitting 9 people into 3 unnamed teams of 3 gives 280. Work out how many times one split like {가,나,다},{라,마,바},{사,아,자} counted in Seoyeon expression. [9 3 280]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.hint.0: List all ways to name teams Team 1, Team 2, Team 3 for one split. [1 2 3]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.hint.1: Compare how to count these when teams unnamed.
y-m-38-04.s.s4.placeholder: Example: This split counted ... times in Seoyeon expression, and ...
y-m-38-04.s.s4.selfAssess.0: I connect why split counted 6 times with 3! ways to name teams? [6 3]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.selfAssess.1: I say when teams have names these 6 count as different cases? [6]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.model.0: Even one split has 3!=6 ways to name teams Team 1,2,3, so named teams count it 6 times. If unnamed, all 6 are same split. Thus 1680÷6=280. 가 나 다 라 마 바 사 아 자 [3 6 1 2 3 6 6 1680 6 280]
y-m-38-04.s.s4.model.1: Seoyeon 1680 counts order of first, second, third chosen team. The 6 (3!) orders of choosing same teams count separately. If teams indistinguishable those 6 become one, so divide by 6 to get 280. [1680 6 3 6 6 280]

y-m-38-06.title: ‘If you choose more, di number of ways go grow too’ always correct?
y-m-38-06.topic: How number of combinations change with number wey person choose, and one counterexample
y-m-38-06.goal: Know say some numbers growing one after another no mean say ‘e always dey grow’; find one r for di table wey di value no grow and use am as counterexample, then predict where di value go reach highest for another n and explain why.
y-m-38-06.material: Fruit get 9 different kinds. Choose r kinds (choice order no matter) make gift box. Number of kinds of box na C(9,r), di number of ways to choose r kinds. Minseo see say for r=0, 1, 2, 3, di values dey grow: 1, 9, 36, 84, then talk say, ‘If you choose one more fruit, di number of box kinds wey you fit make go always grow too.’
y-m-38-06.thinking.0: Judge whether di evidence enough to make general statement
y-m-38-06.thinking.2: Predict using one structure wey get symmetry
y-m-38-06.prereq.0: H1 for dis set na only production difficulty level; e no mean Ministry of Education assign am to one particular class. Assume say you don learn basic counting unit (separate cases to count, count choices one after another, symbols nPr and nCr for permutations and combinations). You sabi wetin number of combinations C(n, r) mean.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.prompt: From wetin you don see so far, wetin be di best judgment about Minseo statement?
y-m-38-06.s.s1.hint.0: Put di range of r wey Minseo check beside all possible r (0 to 9), then compare dem.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.hint.1: Choose one r wey you never check and calculate C(9,r) by yourself.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.o.a: E grow 4 times straight, from r=0 to 3, so we fit take say e go grow for every r.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.r.a: You believe say na rule because you see 4 examples. You still no know wetin happen for r wey you never see.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.o.b: r=0 mean say you choose nothing, so you no fit use dis evidence at all.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.r.b: True say r=0 na special case, but because of dat one you throw away even di other examples.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.o.c: Say e grow 4 times na evidence, but e fit stop for one r wey we never see.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.r.c: Dis judgment accept di examples we don see as evidence, but e point out say some range never get test.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.o.d: If number wey person choose change, di numbers of ways no relate to each other, so comparing dem no get meaning by itself.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.r.d: You fit compare number of ways even if di number wey person choose different. No reason dey to conclude say dem no relate.
y-m-38-06.s.s1.explain: Di 4 examples support di claim, but ‘always’ mean every r. E fit be different for r wey we never see (4 or more), so we need test more.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.prompt: Di C(9,r) values for r=0 to 9, in order, na 1, 9, 36, 84, 126, 126, 84, 36, 9, 1. Find 3 different r wey Minseo statement no work, meaning C(9,r) no bigger pass C(9,r−1) (e equal or smaller).
y-m-38-06.s.s2.hint.0: For di table, pair up two values wey dey side by side and check dem one by one: whether di later value bigger pass di earlier one.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.hint.1: Find di first pair where di later value no bigger pass di earlier one, then check whether everything after am na the same.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.var.r: Number of fruit wey person choose, r
y-m-38-06.s.s2.ok.c1: r na natural number from 1 to 9.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make r be natural number from 1 to 9. (You dey compare with r−1, so you no fit use 0.)
y-m-38-06.s.s2.ok.c2: Di number of ways to choose r kinds no grow compared with choosing r−1 kinds.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.fail.c2: For dis r di value grow. Check di table find where di value stop increasing.
y-m-38-06.s.s2.explain: For r=5, di value na 126, same as r=4 (e no grow); for r=6, 7, 8, 9 e reduce to 84, 36, 9, 1. So r=5, 6, 7, 8, 9 all be counterexamples wey break Minseo statement. r=5 no grow because e ‘equal’; di others ‘decrease.’
y-m-38-06.s.s3.prompt: With 9 fruit kinds, values for r=4 and r=5 equal 126. With 10 fruit kinds, for which r di value go highest? Write your prediction and reason. (Choosing r kinds fit also mean how many ways to leave some unchosen.)
y-m-38-06.s.s3.hint.0: Use small example (choose 1 from 4) check whether each way to choose r go match one by one with di 10−r ones wey remain.
y-m-38-06.s.s3.hint.1: Make some tables to compare C(10,r) for r and 10−r.
y-m-38-06.s.s3.placeholder: Example: With 10 kinds, I think di highest go be at r=... because ...
y-m-38-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: I write both where di value highest and di reason?
y-m-38-06.s.s3.selfAssess.1: I explain say di values get left-right symmetry using di pair ‘choose’ and ‘leave’?
y-m-38-06.s.s3.selfAssess.2: I compare di two equal values wey dey side by side for 9 kinds with di 10-kind case?
y-m-38-06.s.s3.model.0: I think di highest go be at r=5. Choosing r kinds from 10 na di same as leaving 10−r kinds, so values for r=4 and r=6 equal, and di middle one, 5, pair with itself, so two equal values no dey side by side. C(10,5)=252 na di highest.
y-m-38-06.s.s3.model.1: With 9 kinds, di middle na 4.5, so 4 and 5 equal 126. With 10 kinds, di middle na 5, so choosing 5 give di most, and 4 and 6 na pair, so dem get di same value. Di r wey person choose and di 10−r wey remain na pair, so di values get left-right symmetry.
